time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 at t = 0
pixel_convention: x to the right, y downward, full-resolution pixels (1920x1080)

camera.motion: static (no pan/zoom/shake). Seabed skyline (dune crest vs water, x 560..1500) has median per-column shift 0 px vs frame 0 in every frame; per-frame background shift = (0, 0).
camera.view: side view, underwater; shark swims parallel to the image plane (main axis within ~1-2 deg of horizontal, apparent height constant), so one metres-per-pixel scale applies to the shark.

objects.name: shark
objects.description: single great-white-style shark, grey-blue back, white belly, dorsal fin, crescent tail; the only moving object. Snout tip is rendered semi-transparent/faded (lighter grey cap ~40-50 px long in front of the opaque head).
objects.direction: right to left (negative x), horizontal, constant height in image (centre y ~299)
objects.fully_in_view_frames: 15-30 (both snout tip and tail tip inside the image)
objects.partial: frames 0-14: tail cut by right border (snout visible); frames 31-46: snout cut by left border (tail visible)
objects.reference_point: center_x, center_y in shark.csv = horizontal middle of the snout-tip..tail-tip extent and vertical middle of dorsal-fin-tip..lower-tail-lobe extent (stands in for the rig origin / body centre). For partial frames centre is extrapolated from the visible end with the median full length.

full_length_snout_tip_to_tail_tip_px.note: varies with tail beat and with the faint snout edge

height_px_dorsal_fin_tip_to_lower_tail_l.note: y_min ~162-168 (dorsal fin tip), y_max ~428-434 (lower caudal lobe)

objects.name: seabed
objects.description: sandy dunes along the bottom of the frame with animated cyan caustic light patches
objects.note: caustic patches change brightness every frame (lighting, not objects)

objects.name: particles
objects.description: many small bright cyan/white floating specks (marine snow / bubbles), 3-25 px across, all over the water

objects.name: light_rays
objects.description: soft vertical light shafts from the surface (upper image), static

events.event: shark already in motion at first frame, snout entering from right border
tail tip enters view (whole shark in frame)
shark centre crosses image centre x=960
events.detail: center_x 933 at f23, 874.5 at f24; centre ~ x 1005 at f22
snout_x 59 at f30, cut at f31
tail_x 60 at f46; absent at f47

events.note: motion is continuous and leftward over the whole clip; no stops, no direction changes, no contacts or impacts

files.scripts/: all measurement scripts and small json outputs
